subject: Drama
_width_axis_note: Width in drama varies by the range of styles, forms, dramatic contexts, and collaborative and solo devising challenges students engage with. A student at minimum width works within one familiar style or dramatic context; wider students work across multiple styles, forms and increasingly complex dramatic problems.

AC9ADR8C01.minimum_width: Improvise or devise a short drama or interpret a scripted scene using at least one element of drama and one relevant convention; explain how the choices made shape the dramatic action.
AC9ADR8C01.typical_width: Improvise, devise and/or interpret scripted drama using a range of elements and conventions relevant to the style or form; document and justify choices about how elements and conventions shape dramatic action and communicate meaning.
wider: Use play-building to develop a class response to an inquiry question — evaluate how the collaborative devising process shapes and constrains dramatic choices

Work collaboratively to interpret scripted drama: use improvisation to explore characters and relationships, block the performance space, and apply style-specific conventions — evaluate how each decision shapes meaning
Employ Viewpoints to frame questions about dramatic intent and effect — use the questions to make and evaluate creative decisions rather than just reflect after the fact
elaborations: identifying dramatic potential in starting points and using improvisation and processes such as 'mantle of the expert' to develop situations and characters
using play-building to develop scenes as a class response to an inquiry question
working collaboratively to interpret scripted drama — using improvisation to explore characters, applying conventions, blocking space
using Viewpoints to frame questions to interpret, analyse and evaluate dramatic forms, elements, design and conventions
employing voice/vocalisation and movement appropriate to situation, manipulating space and time to heighten tension and shape meaning
using feedback, reflection or evaluation to develop and extend ideas when improvising, devising and/or scripting

AC9ADR8C02.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one element of drama or convention in own work; make at least one documented refinement to the drama based on that evaluation.
AC9ADR8C02.typical_width: Evaluate and refine use of elements, conventions and design to shape dramatic action; use feedback, documentation and reflection throughout the rehearsal process; explain how refinements change what the drama communicates.
wider: Use Viewpoints questions systematically to evaluate own drama — 'What are your intentions?', 'Is the meaning clear?', 'How could elements be used differently to achieve these effects?' — document evaluation and refinement decisions
Adjust performance based on audience response — evaluate how audience feedback reveals the gap between intention and reception
Consider how empathy should be built into the process of creating effects — explore conventions for developing characters and stories from diverse cultural contexts with empathy and care
elaborations: refining drama during rehearsal using feedback, evaluation, documentation and personal reflection using Viewpoints questions
adjusting performance based on audience response to make meaning clear
planning, organising and rehearsing dramatic action to stage devised and scripted drama — arranging theatre technologies and collaborating in rehearsal
considering how and why empathy should be considered when creating effects and communicating intended meaning

AC9ADR8D01.minimum_width: Develop at least one performance skill (vocal or physical) relevant to a selected style or form; describe what improved and how the improvement affects the drama.
AC9ADR8D01.typical_width: Develop vocal and physical performance skills relevant to selected drama styles/forms through sustained practice; experiment with style-specific conventions and techniques; document development using drama terminology.
wider: Develop vocal qualities of projection, clarity and contrast through deliberate work on pace, pitch, dynamics, pause and silence — document how each element changes what the voice communicates
Experiment with conventions associated with a specific style/form (flashback, aside, slow motion, chorus) — evaluate how each convention shapes and sustains dramatic action
Use improvisation to explore techniques for heightening and releasing tension in a specific style — then use insights from improvisation to interpret scripted scenes in that style
elaborations: developing vocal qualities of projection, clarity and contrast through control of pace, pitch, dynamics and use of pause and silence
developing use of the body to communicate through movement, stillness, realistic and non-realistic movement; exploring ways to transition between scenes
experimenting with ways to use conventions associated with a specific style/form
experimenting with elements of drama and stylistic conventions to create, shape and sustain dramatic action through improvisation and basic devising
using improvisation to explore techniques associated with specific styles to heighten and release tension
experimenting with ways to manipulate elements and performance skills to communicate status/power relationships
understanding the importance of and applying respectful relationships and empathy when developing roles and characters

AC9ADR8D02.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one aspect of own or others' drama using feedback; document one specific change made as a result of the reflection.
AC9ADR8D02.typical_width: Use reflection on own and others' drama to inform choices about elements and conventions; seek, accept and respond to feedback; document how reflection changes dramatic choices over time.
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to deepen reflection — 'How did the performer use language/movement to make their character believable?', 'How would you describe the relationships between characters?' — evaluate how the questions reveal things self-observation misses

Reflect on human behaviours and emotions relevant to the drama — explore how to adapt facial expression, posture, gesture, movement and voice to portray age, power or attitude with authentic understanding
Reflect on how performance skills communicate perspectives — investigate how drama can perpetuate or challenge unequal power relationships and evaluate the practitioner's responsibility
elaborations: reflecting independently and in class discussion to evaluate dramatic action and make decisions about future choices
seeking, accepting and responding to feedback — using Viewpoints to develop reflective questions
developing understanding of human behaviours and emotions using appropriate boundaries by recalling and re-enacting past experiences
reflecting on how performance skills communicate perspectives such as challenging unequal power relationships and oppression

AC9ADR8E01.minimum_width: Investigate how at least one drama work uses elements of drama or conventions to communicate ideas or meaning; explain how specific choices connect to the context in which the drama was created.
AC9ADR8E01.typical_width: Investigate drama works across cultures, times or places; analyse how elements and conventions communicate ideas and meaning; explain how historical and cultural context shapes dramatic choices.
wider: Analyse how linear and non-linear narrative is used in drama from diverse cultures — compare what each narrative structure produces for an audience
Research how the impact of time and place shapes dramatic meaning — investigate how a drama from a historical period communicates differently to contemporary audiences than it did originally
Write or record a review of a drama focusing on specific elements and conventions — evaluate how each choice communicates or fails to communicate the intended ideas
elaborations: researching and noticing how the impact of time and place can differ from one period to another, particularly in relation to drama conventions
using Viewpoints to analyse and evaluate performances — asking about ideas expressed, conventions used, how movement was used
writing or recording a review of drama focusing on use of specific elements and conventions
analysing how linear and non-linear narrative is used in drama from diverse cultures

AC9ADR8E02.minimum_width: Identify at least one example of First Nations Australian drama and explain what makes it culturally significant; describe what respectful and culturally responsive engagement looks like in a drama context.
AC9ADR8E02.typical_width: Investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian drama with attention to ICIP rights and protocols; analyse how practitioners use historical and cultural material responsibly; apply ICIP understanding to own drama-making decisions.
wider: Investigate specific examples of how drama practitioners select and use First Nations Australian historical and cultural material to create contemporary First Nations Australian theatre
Investigate cultural appropriation in drama — analyse a specific case, explain what ICIP rights were denied, and evaluate what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Use ICIP protocols to inform decisions about whether ideas from an existing cultural source can be used when developing new drama work — document the reasoning process
elaborations: identifying how diverse First Nations Australian drama can demonstrate culturally responsive approaches to ICIP rights
using ICIP protocols and guidelines to inform decisions about using cultural expressions in new drama work
engaging in activities to understand how to make ethical choices — asking 'Whose story is it?', 'Is this my story to share?'
investigating how drama practitioners use First Nations Australian historical and cultural material to create contemporary theatre
identifying and analysing cultural appropriation and how to avoid it

AC9ADR8P01.minimum_width: Rehearse and perform a drama for an audience using at least one performance skill and one convention relevant to the style or form; reflect on whether the performance communicated the intended meaning.
AC9ADR8P01.typical_width: Rehearse and perform drama using performance skills and conventions relevant to the style/form; collect and use audience feedback to enhance future performance; reflect on how the performance communicated meaning.
wider: Use Viewpoints to ask reflective performance questions — 'What were your intentions?', 'Was meaning clear?', 'What audience feedback suggested it was engaging?' — develop these as tools for performance improvement
Collect and evaluate audience feedback systematically — compare audience reception with own intentions and evaluate the gap

Perform drama that explores First Nations Australian perspectives on identity, resilience or environmental practices — apply ICIP responsibilities and reflect on how respectful relationships and empathy were communicated to the audience
elaborations: performing using conventions relevant to style, suiting choices to the underlying dramatic structure
collecting and evaluating audience feedback to enhance future performance
using Viewpoints to ask reflective performance questions about intentions, meaning and audience engagement
respecting ICIP rights when performing drama that explores First Nations Australian perspectives
reflecting on how respectful relationships and empathy were applied and interpreted by the audience
